artifacts.name: About this indicator
artifacts.summary: Counts public benches and measures how many resting places the area offers per square kilometre and per resident. Benches support walkable, age-friendly neighbourhoods and give people — especially older or less mobile residents — somewhere to rest during hot weather.
artifacts.description: Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: benches · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Statistics
artifacts.summary: Spread, inequality and clustering measures for the area’s benches. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description: Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: benches · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = -0.09. 1 hot-spot and 0 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of benches density (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 21 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over benches density: **High-High** = a dense neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a sparse one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: benches · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots (per capita)
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = -0.03. 0 hot-spot and 3 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of benches per 1,000 residents (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 21 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over benches per 1,000 residents: **High-High** = a well-supplied neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a poorly-supplied one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: benches · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Provision vs population
artifacts.summary: Do benches track where people live? Benches per 1,000 inhabitants against each sub-area’s population. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is an administrative sub-area, plotting its population against its benches per 1,000 inhabitants. Sub-areas low on the vertical axis but high on the horizontal axis are under-served relative to their residents — an equity signal a density map cannot show.

artifacts.name: Provision per capita
artifacts.summary: Benches per 1,000 residents across the sub-areas — provision relative to need. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each administrative sub-area shaded by its number of benches per 1,000 inhabitants, so the colour reflects provision *relative to residents* rather than raw density. A populous sub-area with average density can still read as under-served here. Sub-areas without usable population data are omitted.

artifacts.summary: A gridded density of benches across the area — brighter means more. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area of interest, each cell shaded by how many benches fall within it. It reveals clusters and gaps that individual points can hide.

artifacts.name: Benches density surface
artifacts.summary: A smoothed, continuous density surface of benches (kernel-style). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A kernel-smoothed density of benches: the point counts are blurred into a continuous surface so clusters show as smooth hot regions rather than individual grid cells — a boundary-free complement to the sub-area choropleth and the raw heatmap.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: benches · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Benches per resident (surface)
artifacts.summary: A continuous surface of benches per 1,000 residents — provision relative to need, without administrative boundaries. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Kernel-smoothed benches density divided by population density on the same grid, scaled to per 1,000 residents. Unlike the per-capita choropleth this owes nothing to administrative boundaries, so gradients *within* a district are visible; the trade-off is that it is a smoothed estimate rather than an exact count per area. Cells with fewer than 1 residents are left transparent, because dividing by a nearly empty cell produces a large figure that reflects the arithmetic rather than good provision. Populated cells with no feature within reach are drawn in the lowest class, not left blank — they are the worst-served places and the reason to read this map.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: benches · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Distance to nearest bench
artifacts.summary: How far to the nearest bench from anywhere in the area (metres). Darker = further. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area, each cell shaded by the straight-line distance to the nearest bench. Dark cells are the furthest from any feature — the access gaps. Straight-line (not routed), so it is an optimistic lower bound; it needs no routing service.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: benches · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Data currentness
artifacts.summary: How recently each bench was last edited in OpenStreetMap (median 2 yr ago). Darker = longer since the last edit. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is a feature, shaded by the number of years since its last OpenStreetMap edit (measured against the data snapshot). Clusters of dark points mark areas where the OSM picture is ageing and may warrant a re-survey — a spatial companion to the data-quality note.
